item.title: Remembrance Day 2026
item.description: On Remembrance Day, we observe a minute of silence in honour of the moment the guns fell still across Europe 108 years ago.Amid the trauma, exhaustion and indeed elation that marked the end of the Great War, that silence held the hope that the world would never again know such horror.More than a century on, it is a hope we are yet to realise, but we hold on to it with every fibre of our being.It is a hope embodied by generations of Australians who have served in our name, and Remembrance Day…

item.title: Remarks - Changi Chapel, Singapore
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Today on Remembrance Day, we pause to honour all who have served in Australia's name. We remember the 108 years ago when the guns fell silent in Europe. Since then, Australian men and women have continued to wear our uniform to defend our democracy and our way of life. The 15,000 Australians who were interned here in Changi represent the best of the Australian character. They showed courage, selflessness, sacrifice, and mateship.

item.title: Advancing Australia's national interest
item.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will travel to Türkiye, the Philippines and China to advance Australia’s economic interests while advocating for peace, stability, and free trade.Prime Minister Albanese will attend the COP31 World Leaders’ Summit in Antalya before travelling to Manila for the 6th ASEAN–Australian Summit and 21st East Asia Summit. The Prime Minister will then travel to China to attend the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen and the Australia–China Annual Leaders’…

item.title: Press conference - Parliament House, Canberra
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good afternoon. Thanks for joining us. I'm joined by the Deputy PM, Richard Marles, and the Home Affairs Minister, Tony Burke. When it comes to the generational opportunity that artificial intelligence offers Australia, I've been very clear. Our task is to make sure that we shape AI rather than AI shape us. It will have a drastic impact on the way that work occurs, on the way that we engage with each other, on the way that society functions.

item.title: Strengthening Australia against AI-driven cyber incidents
item.description: The Albanese Government is today releasing the recommendations of the Rapid Review into the OpenAI agent infiltration of an Australian Government health website.The Review was commissioned in September after OpenAI informed the Australian Government that a rogue AI agent had infiltrated government websites, including the Medicare Statistics Reporting Service Portal.As we said at the time – and made clear to the CEO of OpenAI, Sam Altman – this incident was unacceptable, the disclosure was…

item.title: New Australian AI safety and security protections
item.description: The Albanese Government will enshrine world leading mandatory Artificial Intelligence safety and security protections in Australian AI Standards legislation.Australia has the chance to secure and shape the generational opportunities of AI – in Australia’s national interest – while keeping Australians safe.We want AI investors to come to Australia but first and foremost we want to keep Australians safe. That is why we are choosing to announce our approach to safety first and before a range of…

item.title: Press conference - National Situation Room
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Thanks so much for joining us in the National Situation Room here at NEMA, a proud creation of our government that is making an enormous difference. I'm joined by Kristy McBain, the Minister for Emergency Management, Pat Hetherington, the NEMA Interim Coordinator-General, and Simon Louis from the Bureau of Meteorology.

item.title: Preparing for high-risk weather season
item.description: As the bushfire season and supercharged El Niño event begins to impact parts of Australia, the Australian Government is investing an additional $12 million to strengthen bushfire risk management and support the mental health and wellbeing of emergency first responders.The investment will go towards improving the Australia Fire Danger Rating System (AFDRS) and extending three critical national services that provide bushfire and mental health support.Included in the funding is:

item.title: Press conference - Victoria Barracks Sydney
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good afternoon. I'm very pleased to be joined by the Deputy Prime Minister and the Defence Minister Richard Marles here at this historic site of Victoria Barracks. And today, I can announce that Victoria Barracks will be free for all Sydneysiders to enjoy, and it will remain in public hands. This will give an assurance to the public that the heritage at this site is vital, that it be not just maintained, but indeed enhanced.

item.title: First update on the Defence Estate Audit
item.description: The Albanese Government is acting on the independent Defence Estate Audit, and progressing the most significant reform to Australia’s Defence estate in our nation’s history.Keeping Australians safe is the Government’s priority, and as part of that we must ensure the Australian Defence Force (ADF) has access to facilities that are fit for purpose.In response to the independent Audit, the Government agreed to divest or partially divest 67 sites that were underutilised by Defence, not…

item.title: Departmental ministerial appointment
item.description: The Governor-General has accepted my recommendation to appoint Senator the Hon Tim Ayres, Minister for Industry and Innovation and Minister for Science, to administer the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet (PM&C).This appointment reflects Minister Ayres’ role contributing to oversight of the Office of Artificial Intelligence, which is designing world-leading national AI standards to ensure Australians can share the benefits of this transformative technology, safely, and that AI works…

item.title: Commonwealth Heads of Government 2026 statement between the UK and Australia
item.description: Addressing online violence in our democracies – promoting equality in Commonwealth Parliaments.A toxic online environment is a threat to all Commonwealth democracies. It threatens our values and undermines our people’s freedom and choices. Workplace violence in any context is unacceptable, including that faced by journalists and media who are crucial to protecting freedom and democracy. We also condemn rising violence and aggression towards all frontline workers, including health and retail…

item.title: Press conference - Saint John's, Antigua and Barbuda
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: It's been a really productive day here at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting. CHOGM, of course, brings together 56 nations, representing a third of the world's population and representing a significant portion of the world's GDP. It, of course, has been concentrating on the issue of the global economy and international trade. And I've taken the opportunity to advance Australia's national interests, which is why we engage with our interconnected world.

item.title: CHOGM Joint Forums and side events official launch
item.description: Your Excellency Sir Rodney Williams, Governor-General of Antigua and Barbuda, and Lady Sandra Williams.The Right Honourable Gaston Browne, Prime Minister of Antigua and Barbuda, and Minister Maria Browne.Your Excellencies, Heads of Government and Heads of Delegation.The Honourable Shirley Botchwey, Commonwealth Secretary-General.It is a great pleasure to be here in Antigua and Barbuda.And to join friends from across the Commonwealth.This means friends from every continent, many cultures and…

item.title: Commonwealth Nature Initiative side event
item.description: The Right Honourable Gaston Browne, Prime Minister of Antigua and Barbuda.Your Excellencies, Heads of Government, Heads of Delegation, Honourable Ministers.Our host Dr Andrew Forrest.Business and nongovernment organisation leaders.It’s a pleasure to be here, on the Green Pioneer, for a green pioneer – to honour the environmental leadership of His Majesty The King.Protecting and restoring nature is a global, intergenerational compact.And that is the ambition at the heart of the Commonwealth…

item.title: Press conference - Saint John's, Antigua and Barbuda
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: This morning I had the great honour of giving the keynote address at the opening of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting here in Antigua. The Commonwealth is an important institution of which Australia has played an important historical part. 56 countries representing one third of the world's population, 2.7 billion people. The combined economies will be pretty close to $30 trillion dollars next year. That represents a double of what it was just a…

item.title: 2027 WA Australian of the Year Awards
item.description: What you see on this stage is the best of what being an Australian looks like.It is people who tell our national story through action.And they tell our national story through the compassion they have for Australians that they will probably never meet themselves.And a lot has changed over the last five years.But I've had the joy of being responsible for helping with the National Australia Day Council for five years, and something I learned really early on, which remains as true today as it was…

item.title: 2026 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting
item.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will travel to Antigua and Barbuda to attend the 2026 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) from 31 October to 4 November 2026.Representatives from over 50 countries are expected to attend the meeting to discuss shared challenges and opportunities under the theme of Accelerating Partnerships and Investment for a Prosperous Commonwealth.The Commonwealth is a unique and diverse grouping of 56 countries, representing 2.7 billion people from both advanced…

item.title: Press conference - Canberra
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good morning. This has been a big week in parliament. Yesterday, the House of Representatives passed the Digital Duty of Care legislation. It is vital that this get the support of the Senate. It does two things essentially, the first is it makes big tech accountable. Just as the media organisations represented here are accountable for what’s on their platforms, they should be held to account for the role that they play and what appears on their platforms and…

item.title: National Veteran Employment Awards
item.description: I begin by acknowledging the Traditional Owners of the land on which we meet and I pay my respects to their elders past, present and emerging.Thank you, Aunty Serena Williams, for that beautiful welcome to country.I’d like to acknowledge all our distinguished guests, including my colleagues from across the Parliament.I especially want to thank the veterans and serving personnel of the Australian Defence Force and the families who provide them with support.

item.title: National Police Bravery Awards
item.description: I begin by acknowledging the Traditional Owners of the Land on which we meet, and I pay my respects to Elders past, present and emerging.I would also like to acknowledge:Scott Weber, CEO of the Police Federation of AustraliaKrissy Barrett, Commissioner of the AFPAnd all other distinguished guests, including my colleagues from across the Parliament.I would especially like to acknowledge all police officers here with us tonight – and on behalf of the nation, I thank you.

item.title: Veteran employment awards celebrate success beyond service
item.description: Supporting the long-term wellbeing of veterans and their families is a key focus of the Albanese Government.The Royal Commission into Defence and Veteran Suicide identified the transition from full-time ADF service to civilian life as a key pressure point for many in the veteran community.A good job with a supportive employer can ease that pressure and underpin a successful transition for veterans and families of veterans.

item.title: The Australian Workers' Union 2026 National Conference
item.description: I begin by acknowledging the traditional owners of the land on which we meet and I pay my respects to their elders past, present, and emerging.To National Secretary, Paul Farrow, National President Marina Chambers, National Executive Members, Elected Delegates, and Rank and File Members.Thank you for this opportunity to acknowledge the great support of the AWU.Paul invited me personally and I was delighted to accept.It’s been a privilege to get to know Paul in recent years.

item.title: Digital duty of care
item.description: Well, thanks very much, Mr. Speaker.For several years now, Australians have been increasingly concerned about the impact of the online world on the welfare of children and on the cohesiveness of our society.A movement for change, begun and led by brave parents who saw their children's lives taken by cruel and highly addictive social media, created a remarkable period of bipartisanship that put Australia in the forefront of global movements to bring about online safety.

item.title: Western Sydney goes international
item.description: The first international arrival to Australia’s newest full-service airport has touched down, with Air New Zealand NZ165 from Auckland landing at Western Sydney International (Nancy-Bird Walton) Airport earlier this morning.After a short stopover, a full flight was boarded for the return leg and NZ166 departed. This is the first of three weekly return flights between Western Sydney International Airport (WSI) and New Zealand’s largest city.

item.title: Helen Haines - Parliament House, Canberra
item.description: As the House meets for the first time since the horrific events of last Monday, it is appropriate that our very first act is to speak about the Member for Indi, Dr Helen Haines.Her husband, Phil Haines, is with us this morning. He has shown a level of grace that, for most of us, is simply beyond reckoning.This morning Phil spoke lovingly of Helen’s superpowers as empathy, kindness and compassion.He spoke of hope and change, and the need for a gentler, more cohesive path.

item.title: Opening of Western Sydney International Airport
item.description: I begin by acknowledging the Traditional Owners of the land on which we meet, and I pay my respects to Elders past, present and emerging.I’d like to thank and Wurundjeri Elder Jason Tweedie for the smoking ceremony, and John Terrick for that wonderful yidaki performance.I would also like to acknowledge Her Excellency Governor Margaret Beazley, Western Sydney International chair Paul O’Sullivan, Western Sydney CEO Simon Hickey, Premier Chris Minns, and all my colleagues from across federal and…

item.title: First passengers lift off from WSI
item.description: At 11am Australian Eastern Daylight Time, JQ362 will take off from Western Sydney International (Nancy-Bird Walton) Airport, the first passenger flight for this brand new Airport.Hundreds of spectators will also be in attendance as the full capacity Jetstar Airbus A320 takes off for the maiden passenger voyage, connecting Western Sydney to the Gold Coast for the first time.

item.title: Australia's first major new airport has been decades in the making
item.description: This weekend, history will be made in Western Sydney.On Sunday, the first domestic flight will take off from Western Sydney International Airport. And on Monday, the first international flight will do the same.For the first time in more than 50 years, Australia is opening a major new airport.It’s a milestone that has been decades in the making and one that belongs to the people of Western Sydney.For generations, Western Sydney has been a place where people come to build a better life for…

item.title: Hellenic Club Centenary Gala Ball
item.description: I begin by acknowledging the Traditional Owners of the land on which we meet, and pay my respects to Elders past, present and emerging.I would also like to thank your President, Nick Hazistergos, for asking me to be part of this landmark moment in the Hellenic Club’s history.It is such a joy to be with you tonight to celebrate 100 years of the Hellenic Club, Sydney.To crack a century is never a matter of mere luck.The Hellenic Club is a story written in the ink of belief, determination and hard…

item.title: Future Brisbane
item.description: Well, thanks very much, Jonesy, for the invitation to celebrate with you 10 years, a whole decade of dealing with Future Brisbane and being such a strong advocate for this great city and the way that the Courier Mail plays such a strong role.

item.title: Funding for world-class Gold Coast sports facility
item.description: The Gold Coast will be home to a new world-class facility with a strong focus on supporting women, girls and Para-athletes while creating a sporting legacy for the city.The Gold Coast Titans Community Hub and High Performance Centre in Carrara will bring the NRL and NRLW programs and Titans Netball together in one location, while opening up new facilities for community sport.The Albanese Government will invest $15 million towards the new centre, which will help grow junior participation and…

item.title: Radio interview - ABC Sydney
item.description: HAMISH MACDONALD, HOST: The Prime Minister, Anthony Albanese, is here to talk to you this morning. Good morning, PM.ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good morning, Hamish. Good to be with you.MACDONALD: Obviously, we've had that update from Phil Haines. Do you have anything additional you can let us know about with regards to Helen's condition this morning?

item.title: Radio interview - Nova Perth
item.description: NAT LOCKE, HOST: Prime Minister, good morning.SHAUN MCMANUS, HOST: Good morning, Albo.ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good morning. Good to be with you.LOCKE: You too. I saw that you were in Perth over the weekend for Telethon.

item.title: Radio interview - ABC Perth
item.description: MARK GIBSON, HOST: You never quite know who's going to phone into the breakfast show. Line two, the Prime Minister, Anthony Albanese. Good morning.ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good morning, Mark. 2008, it doesn't seem like that long ago.GIBSON: It doesn't, does it? 16 years ago.PRIME MINISTER: Yeah.

item.title: Radio interview - 2SM Sydney
item.description: CHRIS SMITH, HOST: On the line right now I've got the Prime Minister, Anthony Albanese. PM, welcome to the show.ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good morning, Chris. Good to be with you.SMITH: You would have been listening at least to some of that press conference yesterday. Heartbreaking to hear that she had lost her second leg as well. And she really is in for the fight of her life from here, isn't she?

item.title: We need only look to Helen Haines
item.description: In too many ways, the world is a more dangerous and divided place than it was a generation ago.And often as Australians when we see political violence elsewhere we take pride and comfort in the idea that our democracy is differentMore peaceful, more stable, more respectful.This is why the horrific attack on Helen Haines has so shocked our nation.This was an attack on a hardworking, intelligent and thoroughly decent woman who is beloved in her community – and respected across the Parliament.

item.title: Television interview - News24
item.description: KIERAN GILBERT, HOST: It's been a very tough week for the town of Wangaratta, for the Parliament of the nation, and of course, for the family of Helen Haines as she continues to fight for her life in a Melbourne hospital. To discuss this and all the ramifications of this alleged act of violence against an MP, let's bring in Prime Minister Anthony Albanese. PM, thanks very much for your time. Have you got an update on Helen today?

item.title: Radio interview - ABC Melbourne
item.description: RAF EPSTEIN, HOST: The Prime Minister Anthony Albanese joins us on the line. Good morning, PM.ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good morning, Raf. Good to be with you.EPSTEIN: Have you spoken to Helen Haines or Helen Haines’ family recently, yesterday or today?

item.title: Speech - The Age's Melbourne Assembly
item.description: I begin by acknowledging the traditional owners of the land on which we meet and I pay my respects to their elders past, present and emerging.Thank you to Neary Ty for the warm introduction.I acknowledge the Premier of Victoria, my friend Ben Carroll.Ben takes a huge amount of pride in his city and his state.He knows the suburbs and the regions, and he advocates and delivers for them.Ben and his Government believe in this great state, and in its ability to continue to grow and thrive and lead…

item.title: Television interview - ABC News Breakfast
item.description: JAMES GLENDAY, HOST: We are now joined by the Prime Minister, Anthony Albanese, who is in Sydney for us this morning. Prime Minister, welcome back to News Breakfast.ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good morning, James.GLENDAY: Really appreciate you making time for us. Is there anything at all you can tell us about the state of this investigation and also the condition of Helen Haines?

item.title: Television interview - News24
item.description: PETER STEFANOVIC, HOST: Prime Minister, good to have you with us this morning. Thanks for your time. Do you have any more information on the attack this morning?

item.title: Television interview - Today Show
item.description: SYLVIA JEFFREYS, HOST: It is being described as one of the darkest days in Australian political history. Federal Independent MP Helen Haines struck by a car outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, Victoria, in what's suspected to be a targeted attack.

item.title: Television interview - Sunrise
item.description: DAVID WOIWOD, HOST: Joining us now is Prime Minister Anthony Albanese. Good morning to you, Prime Minister. Of course, our thoughts are with Helen Haines and her family this morning. Do you have any update on her condition?

item.title: Television interview - ABC 7.30
item.description: SARAH FERGUSON, HOST: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese joins me now in the studio. Prime Minister, welcome.ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good evening.FERGUSON: What's the very latest you know about Helen and how she is?

item.title: Press conference - Sydney
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good evening. Tonight, I want to update Australians on a serious incident that has occurred in Victoria. This afternoon, Helen Haines, the Member for Indi, was attacked outside her electorate office in Wangaratta. All of our thoughts are with Helen, her family, her friends, her team, and her community at this extremely difficult time. We are praying for her full recovery. I want to thank the first responders for their extraordinary work. There is a major police…

item.title: 2026 Telethon gala ball
item.description: It is wonderful to be back here again at Telethon.I begin by acknowledging the Traditional Owners of the land on which we're meeting, and pay my respect to Elders, past, present, and emerging.I acknowledge too, the most important people who are involved in tonight's event and the events over the next 36 hours – the kids we're helping, represented by the fabulous little stars that we saw before in the video, Aidan, Olivia, and Paige.

item.title: Albanese Government delivers $6 million to Telethon
item.description: The Albanese Government has committed $6 million to the Channel 7 Telethon Trust for 2026 to help improve the health and wellbeing of Australian babies and children.Telethon is an annual televised fundraising appeal in Western Australia and is broadcast live for 26 hours.For almost six decades, Telethon has raised more than $778 million for sick and disadvantaged children in Western Australia.

item.title: Centenary of parliament sitting
item.description: To mark 100 years since our national parliament first met in Canberra, the 48th Australian Parliament will sit for a day at Old Parliament House in April next year.The special sitting day will see Question Time, legislation and other statements return to the Chambers of Old Parliament House for the first time in decades.In 1927, the “Provisional Parliament” was opened in Canberra and our national parliamentarians continued to meet in that building until 1988.Learning from our democratic history…

item.title: Centenary of the Canberra Times
item.description: Thank you so much, JP.I also join in acknowledging the Traditional Owners of the Land on which we meet, and I pay my respects to Elders past, present and emerging, as well as to all First Nations people with us here this evening.To the Governor-General, Your Excellency, it is wonderful to be with you as well.And I think you are doing an extraordinary job, and I say, more than fulfilling the confidence that I had in you.

item.title: Federation of Ethnic Communities' Councils of Australia national conference
item.description: Thank you so much to Prerana and to Peter for giving us a powerful beginning for this morning's events and discussions. And thank you to Auntie Serena and her niece and nephew for once again giving us a wonderful Welcome to Country. And I join with her in acknowledging the traditional owners of the land on which we're meeting, past, present and emerging. I acknowledge Dr Anne Aly, our fantastic Minister for Multicultural Affairs, and I acknowledge other Members of Parliament, Senators who are…

item.title: Opening remarks - Parliament House, Canberra
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER OF AUSTRALIA: Your Majesty, it is an absolute honour to welcome you to Australia. We had a very good meeting last year in New York, where we discussed the full range of issues confronting not just our nations, but confronting the world and humanity. Unfortunately, some of those are of course, still going because we do live in a time of increasing global uncertainty, particularly with the escalating conflict in the Middle East. We share your condemnation of the…

item.title: Joint leaders' Statement on Enhanced Cooperation
item.description: The Prime Minister of Australia, the Hon Anthony Albanese MP, and His Majesty King Abdullah II ibn Al Hussein of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan met in Canberra on 14 October 2026 and reaffirmed the enduring friendship between Australia and Jordan built on mutual respect and a shared commitment to peace, security and prosperity. Leaders welcomed the opportunity to set a forward-looking agenda for strengthened cooperation, building on the 2016 Joint Declaration on Enhanced Cooperation, and…

item.title: Television interview - ABC Afternoon Briefing
item.description: PATRICIA KARVELAS, HOST: The Prime Minister is my lead guest this afternoon, Anthony Albanese, Welcome to the program.ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Goood afternoon. Good to be with you.KARVELAS: In the last couple of weeks, some Labor MPs have been feeling a little bit nervous. Today you told your Caucus you would be kicking with the wind in the fourth quarter. It's a term you used before the last election I recall –PRIME MINISTER: And the one before.

item.title: Visit to Australia by the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan
item.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will welcome His Majesty King Abdullah II ibn Al Hussein of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan to Australia from 13 to 14 October 2026.Australia and Jordan share a warm relationship, underpinned by defence and security cooperation.Our countries are working together to advance peace and regional security, support humanitarian efforts, to counter terrorism and violent extremism, to grow trade and to strengthen cooperation on resources, energy, and the environment.

item.title: National reflection 25 years of Australian service in Afghanistan
item.description: It is a profound honour to join with you today on this landmark anniversary.I acknowledge Her Excellency, the Governor-General of Australia, Sam Mostyn, I acknowledge the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Defence, Richard Marles, and the Minister for Veterans' Affairs, Matt Keogh. I acknowledge the Leader of the Opposition, and other parliamentarians who are here. I acknowledge former prime ministers' John Howard, Tony Abbott and Scott Morrison.

item.title: 25 years since Australians answered the call in Afghanistan
item.description: Today marks 25 years since the commencement of Operation Slipper, Australia’s first military contribution to the war in Afghanistan and the beginning of a significant chapter in our nation’s military history. In the wake of the 11 September 2001 terrorist attacks in the United States, Australia joined an international coalition to combat terrorism and support security and stability in Afghanistan.

item.title: Vale Richard Morecroft
item.description: I was very sorry to hear of the passing of Richard Morecroft. As the face and the voice of the news of the ABC, Richard became a beloved part of Australian life. Combining a consummate professionalism with an unyielding humanity, Richard was a figure of absolute trust, a warm and familiar presence who guided us through the good times and bad.

item.title: Third anniversary of October 7 attacks
item.description: Today, we pause to remember the devastation that Hamas unleashed in the terrorist attack in Israel on the 7th of October, 2023. On this dark anniversary, we remember the 1200 who were taken from the world, the largest loss of Jewish life on any single day since the Holocaust.We think of everyone who was dragged into captivity, everyone who never returned home to their families, and everyone forever scarred by what they endured.

item.title: Statement on Death of Australian Army Soldier
item.description: Our nation’s thoughts are with the family, friends and colleagues of the Australian Army soldier who has tragically died during a training exercise in the Northern Territory yesterday. Our thoughts are also with the five other Australian Army soldiers who were injured in the incident, and we wish them a speedy recovery. There are no safe or easy days for those who serve in our country's name. This sad incident is a terrible reminder of what families take on when their loved one bravely puts on…

item.title: Doorstop - Nadi, Fiji
item.description: It's wonderful to be here in Fiji and to also be visiting Tuvalu in what is the important meeting leading up to the Climate Change Conference next month. It is important that Pacific voices are heard, because the Pacific is the front line of action on climate change. For many of the nations represented by leaders here, it is literally a threat to their very existence, which is why the world must act. We know that we're seeing more intense and more extreme weather events, more frequent on…

item.title: Pre-COP Leaders’ Event in Fiji and Tuvalu
item.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will travel to Fiji and Tuvalu from 5 to 7 October 2026 for the Pre-COP Leaders’ event. At COP30, Australia secured the role of COP31 President of Negotiations and agreement to deliver a Pacific-hosted Pre-COP, including a special Leaders’ event. Australia will co-host the event with Fiji and Tuvalu.

item.title: Vale Bruce Baird
item.description: With the passing of Bruce Baird, Australia has lost a real gentleman and a true parliamentarian. Bruce had the uncommon distinction of serving his nation as a Liberal member at both the state and federal level, including as Transport Minister in the Greiner NSW Government. It was a portfolio he handled with such aplomb that I was pleased to appoint him years later as the inaugural chair of the National Heavy Vehicle Regulator Board.Then of course there was his glittering success as the minister…

item.title: Press conference - Bell Bay, Tasmania
item.description: JESS TEESDALE, FEDERAL MEMBER FOR BASS: Thank you so much everyone for being here today. I look around and see so many people who have worked tirelessly for months and months for this day to get here. Do you know what? Uncertainty is a terrible thing. For 18 months, the 550 workers here at Bell Bay Aluminium have faced that uncertainty. They've been putting decisions about their future on hold, whether to buy a house, get another dog, or maybe even to start a family. They then had to go through…

item.title: Securing the Future of Bell Bay Aluminium
item.description: The Albanese and Rockliff Governments are securing the future of Bell Bay Aluminium smelter, supporting the facility’s 550 workers, their families and the 1,000 workers indirectly employed across Northern Tasmania. We want to see Australia make more things here.This investment will boost jobs in the region while strengthening our national sovereignty.The Bell Bay smelter is a major contributor to Tasmania's industrial and manufacturing sectors and is vital to the Northern Tasmanian regional…

item.title: Launch of Three Shocks
item.description: I begin by acknowledging the traditional owners of the land on which we meet, and I pay my respects to elders past, present and emerging.It is such a pleasure to be here tonight for the launch of Three Shocks – Who We Are Becoming in the 21st Century.In this age of shrinking attention spans, George Megalogenis stands out as a rarity.With his eye for detail and his capacity for joining the dots, George makes a valuable contribution to the national discourse every time he hits the keyboard.

item.title: Press conference - Footscray
item.description: DANIEL MULINO, ASSISTANT TREASURER: Hi, I'm Daniel Mulino. It's great to be here in Melbourne's west in my electorate for an announcement in relation to a very significant transport and infrastructure project. The Melbourne Airport Rail Link is going to transform transport in the West and also be a major economic contributor to Victoria. This is a project that is long overdue, so it's wonderful to be here today for this announcement.

item.title: Melbourne Airport Rail Stage 2 set for take-off
item.description: The Albanese and Carroll Labor Governments are getting on with building Melbourne Airport Rail Stage 2, with work set to begin in the coming weeks.It will include a new 7.4-kilometre rail line from Albion toward the Airport precinct via a brand-new Keilor East station, as part of the $12 billion joint commitment from the Albanese and Carroll Labor Governments.The line will connect directly to the Metro Tunnel and feature the same high-capacity signalling to enable frequent services.

item.title: Press conference - Adelaide
item.description: CLAIRE CLUTTERHAM, MEMBER FOR STURT: Good morning everyone, my name is Claire Clutterham and I’m the federal Member for Sturt in the Australian Parliament and it is a pleasure to be here this morning at Hampstead Barracks. I’m joined by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Assistant Minister for Defence Peter Khalil, and our South Australian Premier, Peter Malinauskas. And this morning we are talking about an issue that is at the heart of the Federal Government’s agenda and at the heart of the…

item.title: Accelerating the delivery of more homes for South Australians
item.description: The Albanese and Malinauskas Governments are working together to fast-track more housing for South Australians, through the redevelopment of two key Defence sites near the Adelaide CBD.Hampstead Barracks was recently identified as a property for divestment, as part of the Australian Government’s response to the independent Defence Estate Audit. The Audit identified sites surplus to Defence’s need, with no clear or ongoing link to capabilities or keeping Australians safe.

item.title: Radio interview - ABC Northern Tasmania
item.description: DAN TAYLOR, HOST: My first guest this afternoon, it's a bit of a late booking. He joins us, he's the 31st Prime Minister of Australia, Anthony Albanese. Good afternoon.ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: G’day Dan. What a stunning day it is here today.TAYLOR: Oh, isn't it just. And you did a little bit of an update on that $130 million redevelopment of UTAS today. You did a bit of a press conference. How's it looking down there?

item.title: Press conference - Launceston, Tas
item.description: JESS TEESDALE, MEMBER FOR BASS: Welcome everybody to the ground here at UTAS Stadium. We're so excited once again to have our amazing PM back in Launceston. I'm joined by Premier Jeremy Rockliff, and also our Minister for Infrastructure who is critical to what has been happening here at UTAS Stadium over the past 12 months. Now, we can see behind us the stand which will have so many thousands of loving, cheering fans coming out as often as possible, particularly when the Tasmanian Devils do get…

item.title: More fans, closer to the action as new stand opens at Launceston's UTAS stadium
item.description: Work on the new Western Stand at Launceston’s UTAS stadium is now complete. It’s another major milestone on the $130 million development of the facility, funded by the Albanese and Rockliff Governments.The new Western Stand repurposes previously unused space between the stand and the pitch, with the new infill seating giving an extra 1,500 fans a front row seat to the action.Spectators will now enjoy modern facilities with wider concourse areas, improving patron circulation and better match-day…

item.title: Doorstop - Sydney
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Australia is leading on digital safety because we want to keep Australians safe. We're living in an age of artificial intelligence. We want to shape this technology in Australia’s national interest, rather than have it shape us. We now know that it wasn't just the issue of the Australian sites that have been subject to AI agents accessing information without authorisation. There are dozens of cases, including US government sites.

item.title: Television interview - News24 NewsDay
item.description: KIERAN GILBERT, HOST: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, thanks for your time. This Medicare hack, what's the latest advice that you've got for the Australian people as we go to air this Friday? And specifically in terms of the personal, the question over personal data, I know the investigations are ongoing. Have you got any updated advice as to what you know?

item.title: Australia's National Statement - United States, New York
item.description: My dear colleagues.This evening I want to talk about the need for nations to work together on the new challenges we face – climate change, emerging technology and the breakdown of international rules.Eight decades ago, the citizens and leaders of our nations made a solemn promise to future generations.Having known the ‘untold sorrow’ of two devastating global conflicts in their lifetimes, they vowed to work together to prevent another.

item.title: Remarks - New York
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Well, thanks so much for the warm welcome back here to Blackstone. We were able to meet during last year’s UN General Assembly, and I want to thank you, your team, for all the other investors who are joining us here today. I have a very simple message, which is Australia is open for business. We are a great place to invest. We have economic growth that is higher than that of every advanced economy in the world, except for the United States at the moment.

item.title: Australia's place in the Indo-Pacific - 2026 Atlantic Council Global Citizen Awards - New York
item.description: Thank you so much, my friend, Prime Minister James Marape. To John, to guests, to the extraordinary fellow award winners who I share the stage with tonight, to Alex, to Stefano and to Cynthia. I want to thank my brother - a very special man - the Prime Minister of Papua New Guinea. For those who may not know, there are hundreds of languages in Papua New Guinea - more than any other place on earth. It is such a diverse country, and James has brought that nation together and has shown incredible…

item.title: Press conference - New York
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Thanks for joining me. I want to update Australians on an incident in which an artificial intelligence agent has infiltrated an Australian Government website. This incident occurred in June of this year and involved an OpenAI agent gaining unauthorised access into the public-facing Medicare statistics reporting service portal, which is administered by Services Australia. The AI agent accessed both public and non-public files.

item.title: Remarks, Australia-Ukraine meeting
item.description: VOLODYMYR ZELENSKYY, PRESIDENT OF UKRAINE: I’m very thankful to Anthony personally, and we have very good relations. Thank you to your people, the people of Australia, and your team. Thank you for such great support from the very beginning of this war. Australian people have always been on the side of Ukraine. Thank you very much for real support, specific one, military support, energy support, which was absolutely crucial, humanitarian. Thank you very much for the benefit and for your support…

item.title: Agreement on long-term support and cooperation between Australia and Ukraine
item.description: Today Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy signed the Australia–Ukraine Bilateral Security Agreement. The Agreement provides a framework for defence and security cooperation and affirms Australia’s enduring commitment to Ukraine.After more than four years of defending itself against Russia’s unprovoked and unjustified invasion, Ukraine has developed one of the world’s most innovative and agile fighting forces.

item.title: Macquarie Group Climate event
item.description: Thanks, Shemara, for the introduction.And thanks to Macquarie Group for the invitation to say a few words today. – It’s been a great week of recognition for Australia here at the UN.On Monday I was invited to open Climate Group’s Climate Week NYC 2026 program – in acknowledgement of Australia’s leadership in renewable energy and our work with our Pacific partners, drawing attention to their vulnerability to climate change.

item.title: Doorstop - New York
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Today it's been a very good day in New York. This afternoon, I, together with the President of France, Emmanuel Macron, the Prime Minister of Kenya, the Prime Minister of Spain, we launched the Coalition for Children's Rights and Protection in the Age of Artificial Intelligence. And this is just one of the aspects that the world now is debating. There's recognition that a year ago, when we came to New York following our legislation in 2024, we were leading the…

item.title: Shape the digital world or it will shape us
item.description: Coalition for Children's rights and protections in the age of AIUnited NationsNew YorkColleagues,Australia is an acknowledged first mover and world leader in digital safety.Our journey to creating a safer digital world started in 2024 with the world’s first social media ban for children – now adopted by some 20 countries.

item.title: P4M Summit: Partners for Multilateralism, International Law, Peace and Prosperity
item.description: Colleagues, Australia has always been one of the world’s strongest supporters of the United Nations. Our position on its future and the future of global relations is clear – global challenges cannot be solved by countries acting alone. Especially right now, when we are facing one of the toughest periods in modern history. The war in the Middle East, an ongoing land war in Europe, the global inflation crisis, the fuel crisis and the rise of AI are incredibly serious challenges.

item.title: Doorstop - New York
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Artificial intelligence has the potential to improve lives, to strengthen our economy and productivity, and to massively advance science and medical breakthroughs. But humans need to be in control of it. If it’s going to be successful, then we need to make sure that humans are at the centre of everything that occurs.

item.title: Australia-EU meeting 2026
item.description: The President of the European Council, Antonio Costa, the President of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen and the Prime Minister of Australia, Anthony Albanese met on 21 September in the margins of the United Nations General Assembly.Presidents Costa and von der Leyen and Prime Minister Albanese reviewed the progress made in deepening cooperation across many fields since President von der Leyen’s visit to Australia in March 2026:

item.title: Climate Week Keynote Address
item.description: Thank you for the invitation to officially open Climate Group’s Climate Week NYC 2026.It’s great to be here with so many champions of climate action.Your CEO – Helen Clarkson.Your Chair – my friend Mike Rann.And of course, Ed Milliband.Last year my Minister for Climate Change and Energy, Chris Bowen, addressed this gathering with a message of hope about the vast global move towards renewables now underway.Climate Group and Australia have a long and strong relationship, going back to the…

item.title: Australia launches bid for United Nations Security Council seat
item.description: At a time of global uncertainty and major challenges, Australia is an untiring advocate for peace and security. We understand that this is best achieved through international cooperation, which is why we are launching our campaign for a seat on the United Nations Security Council, to serve a two-year term from 2029 to 2030.

item.title: Press conference - United Nations, New York
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: I'm very proud today to be launching Australia’s campaign for a non-permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council for 2029 and 2030. Australia is the best country on earth, and I firmly believe that our best days are ahead of us. And we have an opportunity through this potential seat on the UN Security Council to play a key role in shaping the global issues that really matter to Australians. We’ve been reminded in recent times of how important the…

item.title: Television interview - ABC Insiders
item.description: DAVID SPEERS, HOST: Prime Minister, thanks for talking to us here in Silicon Valley.ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good to be with you and what a fantastic venue to be at.

item.title: Press conference - Apple Park, California
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: It’s fantastic to be here at Apple headquarters in California, and I do want to thank Tim Cook for the invite, firstly, after we spoke in June, but also for getting together the entire executive team. It was a very fruitful discussion that we had, and then to be able to see the latest products is very important as well.

item.title: Working with Apple on online safety
item.description: The Albanese Government is proud to lead the world in efforts to keep children safe online, and today the Prime Minister welcomed the opportunity to meet the Executive Chairman of Apple’s Board, Mr Tim Cook at Apple Park in Cupertino, United States. As an industry leader, Apple has worked to support Australia’s online safety laws and taken additional steps to help protect kids online.

item.title: Doorstop - San Jose, California
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: It’s great to be back in the United States, and I’m looking forward tomorrow to taking up the invitation of Tim Cook, the Executive Chair of Apple, looking particularly at the issue of child safety and new technology. Australia is, of course, a world leader when it comes to dealing with the issues of safety, when it comes to new technology and the digital economy.

item.title: Visit to California and New York
item.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will travel to the United States from Friday 18 September to Thursday 24 September 2026 to visit Apple Headquarters in California and lead Australia’s delegation at the United Nations General Assembly High-Level Week in New York.The Prime Minister will visit Apple Park and meet the Executive Chairman of Apple’s Board of Directors, Tim Cook, to discuss Apple’s new parental-controls for children, in part inspired by Australia’s groundbreaking reform.

item.title: Australia ranked 8th in global gender equality rankings
item.description: Australia has ranked 8th in the World Economic Forum’s 2026 Global Gender Gap Report, breaking into to the top ten and achieving its highest ever ranking for gender equality, out of 148 countries.This result reflects the Albanese Government’s sustained action to improve the lives of women and girls, including lifting wages in female-dominated industries, expanding Paid Parental Leave to six months with superannuation, and making significant investments in women’s health.

item.title: Little wings flying high
item.description: The Albanese Government is providing another $1 million for Little Wings to help seriously ill children in regional communities access the health care they need.The funding will extend the Government’s support for Little Wings for a further two years, helping families across regional NSW, Queensland and the ACT access the specialist health care their children need.The Government will also match every dollar raised by 12-year-old Dusty Langby, who has walked an incredible 540 kilometres from…

item.title: Press conference - Admiralty House
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good morning. Today is an exciting day for an extraordinary Australian. A familiar face to just about every Australian I think, no matter where they live. For several decades, Melissa Doyle AM has beamed in the living rooms right around the country through a distinguished career as a television presenter, an author, and a journalist. But her footprint through our great community spans well beyond that. She is a champion for Australian children, for Australian…

item.title: Appointment of new Chair for National Australia Day Council Board
item.description: The Albanese Government is pleased to announce Ms Melissa Doyle AM as the new Chair of the National Australia Day Council Board.Ms Doyle has had a distinguished career as a television presenter, author and journalist, with more than 30 years of experience.In the 2016 Australia Day Honours List, Ms Doyle was appointed a Member of the Order of Australia, recognising her significant service to the community through roles with a range of charities and in broadcast media.

item.title: 25th commemoration of September 11
item.description: Today marks 25 years since the terrorist attacks of 11 September 2001, which claimed the lives of thousands of innocent people in the United States and from countries around the world.On this solemn day, we remember the 2,977 people killed in New York, Washington DC and in Pennsylvania, including 10 Australians whose lives were tragically cut short far from home.We acknowledge the grief carried by their loved ones. We also honour the courage and selflessness shown in the face of unimaginable…
